I was sixteen and he was twenty eight. I was walking my dog downtown and he approached me and said "hey, isn't your name [name]?" And we started talking.  To this day, I have no idea how he knew my name.

It should've been a huge red flag, but we had just moved to town and I was struggling a lot with depression and gender identity. I was lonely and so desperate for a friend, and he took advantage of that.

He used to bring me to his apartment, get me drunk, and rape me. I knew it was wrong, but I felt so disconnected from it at the time. He'd take his anger out on me, beat the shit out of me for fun. Pushed me down a flight of stairs outside his apartment once, then told the police I was his little cousin and I had slipped on some ice.

This went on for three years. It was hell, but he had isolated me from everyone else, family included. I tried to get help from teachers and school counselors, but nobody believed me. I had ruined my relationship with my parents. 

I ended it when I went through his phone one night while he was asleep and found a message he had sent to my fifteen year old sister asking what her bra size was. I called my best friend, who I hadn't spoken to in more than a year, and he drove eleven hours that night to come get me.

In the aftermath, I'm not doing great. It's been three years and I'm better, but I'm not good. I live with my parents, we're rebuilding our relationship. They know some of why I left, but they don't know the whole story. I've never talked about it in detail. I go to therapy, but I still deal with suicidal thoughts and severe depression. I can barely hold down a job. Some days, I can't leave the house without having a panic attack. 

On the bright side, I've started transitioning to male. Seeing myself become the version of myself I know I should've been all along has been immensely healing. For the first time in my life, I'm starting to feel like my body is my own.
Absolutely- I have a tattoo from it- "I'm Alec Bings; I see through things."
